summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by severe nausea and vomiting. She presented with high blood glucose, an anion gap of 28, and ketonuria, requiring ICU-level care and an insulin infusion. Her DKA resolved within 24 hours, but nausea persisted. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and close monitoring of electrolytes and blood pressure. A urinary catheter was placed due to acute retention, with resolution within 48 hours. The GI team evaluated her for possible outpatient EGD with Botox injection for gastroparesis. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, remained stable on subcutaneous insulin, and was discharged home with no medication changes and follow-up arranged with her GI physician.
